text: Your mind has weaknesses you probably don't even know about.
First, social exclusion: being ignored can threaten our sense of belonging.
That feeling can hurt, even when no one says a word.
Next, mirroring: people often unconsciously copy gestures and expressions.
This Chameleon Effect can help interactions feel more natural.
Then there's scarcity: limited availability can make things seem more desirable.
That's why countdowns and 'only a few left' can influence decisions.
The foot-in-the-door effect starts with a small request.
Agreeing once can make a larger request easier to accept.
But threaten someone's freedom, and reactance may make them push back.
Sometimes, controlling your choices starts by making you feel you have none.
